name: Dominica
prevalence_note: ECCB, Commonwealth of Dominica Police Force (CDPF) & Ministry of National Security 2025-2026: ECCU bank/OTP phishing, advance-fee lottery and inheritance scams, fake fee-charging immigration/customs portals, and WhatsApp relative impersonation dominate.
cross_border_note: Uses +1-767 within NANP and the ECCU; scammers frequently call from overseas +1 or WhatsApp numbers posing as banks, lottery officials, or travel/customs agents.

scams.name: ECCU Bank Security Alert & One-Time Password Vishing
scams.name_en: Fake bank fraud officer requesting OTP codes, card numbers, or login verification
scams.signals_en: Caller claims to be from a commercial bank in Dominica alerting of suspicious account activity and requesting an SMS code, card CVV, or login through an emailed/texted link.
scams.legit_en: ECCB-supervised banks in Dominica never phone or text customers to ask for passwords, PINs, or one-time verification codes.
bait_tactics: Tell them you will walk down to the Roseau branch in person to verify your account status.
Say your phone battery is almost flat and ask for their department so you can call the main bank switchboard back.
Pretend the SMS code is unreadable on your cracked screen.

scams.name: Advance-Fee Lottery Prize & Unlicensed Crypto Pyramid Scam
scams.name_en: ECCB-warned fake lottery win or zero-risk crypto recruitment scheme demanding upfront payment
scams.signals_en: Caller announces a surprise sweepstakes prize requiring upfront clearance fees, or pitches an unlicensed investment/pyramid club converting funds to cryptocurrency.
scams.legit_en: ECCB warns citizens never to pay fees to claim prizes and to verify investment licences with the ECSRC before sending funds.
bait_tactics: Ask them to deduct the clearance charge from the prize payout and mail a certified bank draft.
Request their ECSRC regulatory licence status so you can check the official register.
Pretend you are searching for a pen and ask them to repeat the company registration details slowly.

scams.name: Fake Immigration / Customs Fee & WhatsApp Relative Scam
scams.name_en: Unauthorized immigration/ED-form or customs parcel fee demand and WhatsApp impersonation
scams.signals_en: Caller or message directs travelers/residents to pay fees for Dominica's free online ED immigration/customs card, pay private accounts for held parcels, or wire urgent funds to a cloned WhatsApp contact.
scams.legit_en: The Government of Dominica levies zero fees for online ED Immigration/Customs forms, and real family emergencies should be verified on known phone numbers.
bait_tactics: Point out that Dominica's official ED form is free and ask which government ministry they claim to represent.
For a family emergency message, call the relative's saved mobile line directly before acting.
Say you will check at the Roseau customs port office in person.
